items.title: Tom Malone interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 3, 2023
items.q: The horn section was Alan Rubin, Lou Marini, Tom Scott, and myself.

ctx.x: Yeah. They changed all the — you know the writers changed all the original lyrics to funny lyrics. And she was delightful. So you never know. I was an arranger for a show called, a TV special called “The Fortieth Anniversary of Atlantic Records.” It was at the Garden, Madison Square Garden. Giant audience. And it was a 14-1/2 hour concert. It started at 10 in the morning and went ‘til 2:30 in the morning. The closing act was Led Zeppelin, who had not performed for six years. Anyway, everybody in the history of…

ran out in the street. So now there’s a girl behind the counter. “Do you play an instrument?” “Yes.” “What do you play?” “Alto sax.” “You want to sit in with the Letterman — do you have your horn with you?” “Yeah it’s right here.” “You want to sit in with the Letterman band?” “When?” “Right now.” “Sure.” So the camera’s following her up Broadway to 52nd Street to the studio and she comes up on the stage and Paul says, “What songs do you know?” She says, “Well I don’t know any songs by ear but if you can write…
